n: Adding to earlier Church laws, the Lord explains how to care for women and children who have lost husbands or fathers—a concern of God’s people in every age.
Wives have a right to be supported by their husbands while the husbands live. If a woman is widowed and remains faithful, she keeps full fellowship in the Church.

f.g: A rightful demand; a just right to receive something.

n: If she is not faithful she loses Church fellowship, yet she may still keep her land and home as the civil law allows. The Church did not strip widows of property.

f.g: Land assigned to members under the law of consecration.

n: Every child has a right to be provided for by his or her parents until reaching adulthood.

f.g: Old enough to be legally an adult.

n: When parents can’t provide an inheritance, children then have a claim on the Church—that is, on the Lord’s storehouse.
Members’ consecrated offerings keep the storehouse supplied, so widows, orphans, and the poor are cared for. True religion has always included this.
